title: Acceleration information and continuum-corrected displacement bounds
post_run_amendment: After the initial study, add explicit finite-coefficient and sampling-lattice guards and project the nonnegative quadratic coefficient upward to zero if the numerical solver returns a tiny negative value. Recompute the full certificate using the projected coefficient. No observation, seed, objective, or development gate changes. The original source, protocol, and results are preserved in work/spectral-response-v1-2026-09-15 outside the portable vault.
status: Development benchmark. Specification follows a prior-art screen and noiseless grid-LP/continuum-certificate development; fixed before this program's stochastic inference examples and calibration audit. Not an external preregistration, held-out discovery test, or novel moment-optimization method.

physical_target.realization: dv=-y dt; dy=(kappa*v-nu*y)dt+sqrt(2*kappa*nu)dW; stationary covariance diag(1,kappa)

confidence.method: Exact chi-square variance intervals for (v0 +/- vk)/sqrt(2), Bonferroni over 38 intervals; independent one-sided chi-square upper acceleration variance. Their intersection has at least 95% coverage of the true entire spectral measure under the stated Gaussian observations.

observable: J(T)=int_0^T (T-t)C(t)dt=int (1-cos(omega*T))/omega^2 rho(domega). J is the mean displacement under a unit step force for the linear target, or the linear-response coefficient for a general equilibrium model. MSD=2J. Bounds concern ensemble functionals, not prediction intervals for an individual trajectory.
spectral_class: All probability measures on nonnegative continuous frequency with sampled cosine moments in simultaneous covariance intervals; acceleration modes additionally impose integral omega^2 rho <= kappa_upper. This is an outer relaxation of a specified free GLE class, not an assertion that every extremal spectral measure has the target's memory structure.
certification: Optimize a cosine-plus-nonnegative-quadratic upper bound for +/-J integrand. For the upper J bound, integer-horizon frequency folding extends a certificate on [0,pi/Delta] to all frequencies, also with an acceleration constraint. For the lower J bound with acceleration information, impose a sufficient tail inequality at tail_start. Refine each finite interval and shift the constant by worst nodal violation plus a proved second-derivative interpolation allowance. These are analytic global certificates evaluated in floating point, not interval-arithmetic proofs. Unknown-acceleration lower infimum is exactly zero.
baseline: Within observed horizons, integrate the piecewise-linear VACF with covariance interval endpoints, then add/subtract kappa_upper*T^2*Delta^2/24. No extrapolation baseline claimed outside the observed window.

development_gate.interpretation: A pre-stochastic-run development screen only. Failure is retained; success would not establish novelty, transfer, equal acquisition cost, or optimality.

cost_scope: Acceleration calibration adds 256 independent scalar readings and access to a different observable. This is an information-addition comparison, not a matched-hardware or matched-cost advantage over more velocity trajectories.
validation: Analytic target versus spectrum and matrix integrals; exact Gaussian covariance interval law; independent calibration audit; primal-dual weak-duality checks on finite grids; continuum corrections; wider moment intervals cannot improve exact optimum; high-frequency tails not silently discarded; truth and baseline inclusion; a refinement subset.
limits: No new theory or algorithm is claimed.
The singular fractional kernel in Benchmark 011 has infinite acceleration variance and is excluded from the finite-sum-rule class.
Known variance, Gaussianity, independent trajectories, ideal instantaneous readings, and transfer of the acceleration calibration are explicit assumptions.
Ordinary resampling on the same time lattice cannot remove the demonstrated high-frequency alias ambiguity.
A confidence set for all spectra gives simultaneous functional coverage; numerical evaluated horizons are not the whole continuum of time unless a uniform time certificate is separately supplied.
